<div class="hmi-analyte-explorer" id="hmi-occurrence-swordfish" data-analyte-explorer data-compact-intro="true" data-source-summaries="true"><details class="hmi-drawer-disclosure" data-explorer-context><summary data-open-context aria-haspopup="dialog" aria-controls="hmi-occurrence-swordfish-drawer">Comparison methods and scope</summary><div data-explorer-context-content>

<p>Each row is one statistic a source reports for one form of swordfish, group and metal; percentiles, ranges and maxima reported for the same samples as a mean or median are shown on that row. Different forms and preparation states are kept apart, and dry-weight results never share a reference with as-sold or fresh-weight results. Ratings place a result against an HMI reference built from monitoring results and ordinary-setting medians for the same form and basis. Same-study contrasts compare a contaminated or treated site with its control, targeted with random sampling, a prepared form with the unprocessed one, or one group of a study with the median of its other groups. Held rows failed a check against their own source and are shown but not compared.</p>

Distribution of subgroup median concentration values.</p><div class="hmi-drawer-table"><table><thead><tr><th scope="col">Reference (µg/kg)</th><th scope="col">Q1</th><th scope="col">Median</th><th scope="col">Q3</th></tr></thead><tbody><tr><td>Primary HMI reference</td><td>≤4.35</td><td>≤20</td><td>25</td></tr><tr><td>Alternative weighting</td><td>≤4.35</td><td>≤20</td><td>25</td></tr></tbody></table></div><p>37 reference units; 3 sampling families. Counts describe evidence units, not independent studies or certainty.</p><div class="hmi-drawer-table"><table><thead><tr><th scope="col">Contributing family</th><th scope="col">Reference units</th><th scope="col">Weight</th></tr></thead><tbody><tr><td>WHO GEMS/Food</td><td>35</td><td>33%</td></tr><tr><td>Olmedo et al. 2013</td><td>1</td><td>33%</td></tr><tr><td>Smolikova et al. 2016</td><td>1</td><td>33%</td></tr></tbody></table></div><p class="hmi-drawer-section-title" role="heading" aria-level="3">Methods</p><p>HMI pools subgroup medians for swordfish, as sold on a as sold, as eaten or fresh weight basis: monitoring results summarized as one median per reporting region, sampling type and collection year, total diet composites and printed sample values as single observations, and printed subgroup medians from ordinary farms or markets. Each sampling family has equal total weight. Non-detects stay as zero-to-limit intervals, so quartiles carry lower and upper bounds. Means, ranges and maxima never enter as observations. Other forms, other bases, targeted sampling and results from mining, industrial, wastewater-affected, experimental, fertiliser or manufacturer settings are kept out of this reference.</p><p>Inverse weighted empirical CDF; midpoint at exact cumulative-weight boundaries. At least four reference units and a definitely positive Q1 to Q3 spread are required. This is a display eligibility rule, not statistical validation.</p><p class="hmi-drawer-section-title" role="heading" aria-level="3">Limitations</p><p>3 sampling families with different designs; none is a probability sample of world supply. Reporting regions and purchase markets are not growing areas. Non-detects with differing limits widen the bounds. A position is descriptive concentration, not a safety or compliance judgment.</p><p class="hmi-drawer-section-title" role="heading" aria-level="3">Admitted source families</p><ul><li><a href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants" class="internal" data-slug="sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants" data-no-cite-meta>WHO GEMS/Food</a></li><li><a href="../sources/olmedo2013-andalusia-fish-shellfish-metals" class="internal" data-slug="sources/olmedo2013-andalusia-fish-shellfish-metals" data-no-cite-meta>Olmedo et al. 2013</a></li><li><a href="../sources/smolikova2016-heavy-metals-fish-czech" class="internal" data-slug="sources/smolikova2016-heavy-metals-fish-czech" data-no-cite-meta>Smolikova et al. 2016</a></li></ul><details class="hmi-drawer-disclosure"><summary>Reference version and interpretation</summary><p>Frozen evidence selection: 2026-10-22. Corrections, completed searches, new direct evidence and changes in requirements should reopen the relevant answer.

## Swordfish FAQs

<details class="qa" data-hmi-faq="1" id="what-heavy-metals-are-found-in-swordfish" data-anchor="what-heavy-metals-are-found-in-swordfish" data-question="What heavy metals are found in swordfish?">
<summary><span class="mk" aria-hidden="true"></span>What heavy metals are found in swordfish?</summary>
<div class="ans" data-hmi-faq-answer="1">

The library reports lead, cadmium, total arsenic, inorganic arsenic, dimethylarsinic acid, total mercury, methylmercury, mercury, chromium, tin, Cu, Se, Se(IV), Se(VI), SeCys, SeMet and tSe in swordfish, most often lead, cadmium and total arsenic.<sup class="cite">[[sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants|1]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">World Health Organization · 2026</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">GEMS/Food Contaminants database heavy-metal exports</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">GEMS/Food Contamination Monitoring and Assessment Programme</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">Read source →</a></span></span></sup><sup class="cite">[[sources/digoarachchi2022-swordfish-yellowfin-tuna-sri-lanka-heavy-metals|2]]<span <details class="qa" data-hmi-faq="1" id="which-regions-report-the-lowest-levels-in-swordfish" data-anchor="which-regions-report-the-lowest-levels-in-swordfish" data-question="Which regions report the lowest levels in swordfish?">
<summary><span class="mk" aria-hidden="true"></span>Which regions report the lowest levels in swordfish?</summary>
<div class="ans" data-hmi-faq-answer="1">

Among GEMS/Food reporting regions, swordfish, as sold had the lowest cadmium subgroup median in EURO (41.5 µg/kg) and the highest in EURO (53 µg/kg); reporting regions are markets, not growing areas.<sup class="cite">[[sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants|1]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">World Health Organization · 2026</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">GEMS/Food Contaminants database heavy-metal exports</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">GEMS/Food Contamination Monitoring and Assessment Programme</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">Read source →</a></span></span></sup> For total arsenic, the lowest regional median was in EURO (670 µg/kg) and the highest in EURO (1,100 µg/kg).<sup class="cite">[[sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants|1]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">World Health Organization · 2026</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">GEMS/Food Contaminants database heavy-metal exports</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">GEMS/Food Contamination Monitoring and Assessment Programme</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">Read source →</a></span></span></sup>

</div>
</details>

<details class="qa" data-hmi-faq="1" id="how-much-of-the-arsenic-in-swordfish-is-inorganic" data-anchor="how-much-of-the-arsenic-in-swordfish-is-inorganic" data-question="How much of the arsenic in swordfish is inorganic?">
<summary><span class="mk" aria-hidden="true"></span>How much of the arsenic in swordfish is inorganic?</summary>
<div class="ans" data-hmi-faq-answer="1">

Inorganic arsenic, the more toxic form, was measured in 5 results from 2 sources, far fewer than total arsenic.<sup class="cite">[[sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants|1]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">World Health Organization · 2026</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">GEMS/Food Contaminants database heavy-metal exports</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">GEMS/Food Contamination Monitoring and Assessment Programme</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">Read source →</a></span></span></sup><sup class="cite">[[sources/marin2018-valencia-foodstuffs-metals|3]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Marín S, Pardo O, Sánchez A, Sanchis Y, Vélez D, Devesa V, Font G, Yusà V · 2018</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/marin2018-valencia-foodstuffs-metals">Assessment of metal levels in foodstuffs from the Region of Valencia (Spain)</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Toxicology Reports 5 (2018) 654-670</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/marin2018-valencia-foodstuffs-metals">Read source →</a></span></span></sup> Marín et al. 2018 reported inorganic arsenic at 9.7 µg/kg (mean) in swordfish, as sold from Fish and seafood group, Region of Valencia TDS 2010-2011.<sup class="cite">[[sources/marin2018-valencia-foodstuffs-metals|3]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Marín S, Pardo O, Sánchez A, Sanchis Y, Vélez D, Devesa V, Font G, Yusà V · 2018</span><a class="cite-card-title"
